name: a_sector_internet_media
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: Company news: internet, media, gaming and telecom.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Every material company-specific news item for US-listed internet, media, gaming and telecom companies >= $1B in the window, as many as you can find: press releases, 8-K filings, executive changes, activist campaigns, legal settlements, contracts, product launches, guidance, analyst rating/PT changes (firm, old → new), and the stock move. One bullet per company.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **GOOGL** / CNN [Internet & Platforms]
- Google added CNN, Financial Times, Axios and other publishers to its AI news program, which has more than 400 publications; financial terms were not disclosed. (Reuters, Oct 15 12:08 ET)[2]

## **ORCL** [Internet & Platforms]
- Five-year credit-default-swap spreads widened 26 basis points overnight to a record 288 basis points, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence. (Reuters, Oct 15; publish time not stated)[1]

## **AMZN** [Internet & Platforms]
- Five-year credit-default-swap spreads reached record-wide levels, according to LSEG and S&P Global Market Intelligence; no spread figure was provided in the report. (Reuters, Oct 15; publish time not stated)[1]

## **GOOGL** / **META** [Internet & Platforms]
- Five-year credit-default-swap spreads reached record-wide levels for both companies, according to LSEG and S&P Global Market Intelligence; the report did not provide individual spread figures. (Reuters, Oct 15; publish time not stated)[1]

## **CRWV** [AI Infrastructure]
- CoreWeave shares fell 6% in premarket trading on Oct. 15 after falling more than 15% on Oct. 14, while its 2032 debt traded at 77 cents on the dollar; five-year CDS spreads exceeded 1,000 basis points. (Reuters, Oct 15; publish time not stated)[1][10]

## **NFLX** [Media & Entertainment]
- Jefferies initiated coverage at **Buy** with an $85 price target; Netflix shares were up 0.7% in premarket trading. (Yahoo Finance, Oct 15 07:19 ET)[5]

## **ERIC** [Communications & Networking]
- Ericsson reported third-quarter adjusted operating profit before amortization and restructuring costs of 10.1 billion Swedish kronor versus an analyst forecast of 7.87 billion kronor; organic sales rose 7% to 59.5 billion kronor versus a 55.4 billion-kronor forecast. (Reuters, Oct 15; publish time not stated)[6]
- Adjusted EBITA margin was 17.0% versus a 14.2% forecast and 28.1% a year earlier; CEO Per Narvinger said component costs were expected to pressure gross margin, while the RAN market was flat. (Reuters, Oct 15; publish time not stated)[6]

## **RELX** [Media & Information Services]
- RELX rose 2.6% in premarket trading to $37.87 after Bank of America Securities reaffirmed **Buy** and a 4,000-pence price target. (Investing.com, Oct 15 07:44 ET)[10]
